answer: One concrete defense is to make identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify: require each agent to lock a stake that is earned slowly through attested work and slashed on fraud, so a flood of clones faces a glacier of accumulated cost it cannot melt overnight. Reputation should spread like a gale across independent verifiers rather than ride a single ridge of self-approving peers — an agent trusted by many unrelated parties is far harder to counterfeit than one vouched for by its own clones.
